content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim against the record. The root-cause line about no minute of the window departing from baseline is backed by the T6 entry and the "not broken" note, and the claim that the record shows no failure mechanism also holds. The plain-words version, that the alarm fired while the measurements looked fine, matches T6. I'm now weighing the still-at-risk claim, that the same alarm could fire again during normal operation, which is a hedged possibility and needs to be checked against what the record shows about the rule firing without a failure.

I'm going through the remaining claims. The symptom line says nobody saw anything wrong, which is a little strong, but "no impact to report" backs it up, so I'll accept it. The chain and the went-wrong point, that nobody was paged, both check out against the changes and the "Nobody was paged" line.

supported.quote: The evidence does not show why the HighErrorRate rule fired: no minute of the window read, including the rule's own series, departed from the service's baseline.
rows: Not broken: the alarm was disproven

supported.quote: So the record shows no failure mechanism behind the alarm.
An error alarm for the shop service went off even though the service's own measurements showed nothing wrong, and the record does not show why the alarm went off.
The same alarm could fire again while the service is working normally.
Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong; an error-rate alarm fired with no matching errors
rows: Not broken: the alarm was disproven

supported.quote: Nobody using io-shop was seen to have any problem. What was seen instead was the HighErrorRate alarm saying the error rate was above its threshold, while the metrics read showed no such errors.
rows: Not broken: the alarm was disproven

supported.quote: The rule fired but the service did not fail: across errors, p50, p95, p99, memory and the alert rule's own series, no minute of the window read departed from baseline.
The record does not show why the rule fired.
Deploys and flags were not read, so no change was tied to the alarm and none was ruled out.
rows: Deploys not read; flags not read.

supported.quote: The alert was not linked to an on-call incident, so nobody was paged by it.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
